extracted.intended_audience: Experts invited to act as peer reviewers for BBSRC research grant proposals (UK and overseas academics, government and industry reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing peer reviews of BBSRC standard research grant proposals, covering procedural expectations, assessment standards, anonymity/conflict policies, and special considerations (e.g., COVID-19, use of AI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: provide BBSRC, when requested, with a review by the due date specified and in accordance with the reviewer guidance in the UKRI Funding Service
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must be provided by the specified due date. See the reviewer form in the UKRI Funding Service for specific guidance on completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification if unable to review
rubrics_metrics.description: notify BBSRC when you are unable to meet a review request by declining via the Funding Service within five working days of the request, so that an alternative reviewer can be sought without delay
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot undertake the review, decline within five working days via the Funding Service to allow timely replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to UKRI policies and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: adhere to and uphold UKRI’s policies, standards and guidance in support of good research practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to follow UKRI policies (including counter fraud/bribery and other relevant standards). Links to UKRI policies are provided for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics (DORA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist’s contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in line with UKRI’s commitment to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA). Assess the content and contributions themselves rather than relying on journal metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional use of linked external materials and anonymity risk
rubrics_metrics.description: In some instances, the proposal may include a link to a website containing information on the research proposed. Reviewers are not required to consider this additional information when providing comments on a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do choose to look at linked external material, note that it is possible that your anonymity to the applicant may be compromised. You may therefore choose not to consult such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using generative AI to develop assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and panellists are not permitted to use generative AI tools to develop their assessment, including to correct language, spelling, grammar and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using generative AI tools can potentially compromise the confidentiality of applicants’ ideas. See UKRI policy on the use of generative AI for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone must be balanced, objective and non-confrontational
rubrics_metrics.description: The tone and language used by a reviewer is confrontational or emotive (is a reason for unusable reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviews must be balanced and objective. Confrontational or emotive language can make reviews unusable and hinders applicants’ ability to respond effectively in the right to reply process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer anonymity (do not identify yourself)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer identifies themselves within their comments (inadvertently or overtly) (is a reason for unusable reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants do not have sight of reviewer identities. Avoid including identifying information in your comments to protect reviewer anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient detail and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer’s comments are too brief (is a reason for unusable reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels need a clear idea of strengths and weaknesses. Comments should be sufficiently detailed and justified so the moderating panel can make an informed decision based on the expert peer reviews received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address expected areas and provide critical examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer has not addressed the areas expected for effective peer review and there is little or no critical examination of the proposal (is a reason for unusable reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective peer review should identify both strengths and weaknesses. Consider and comment on research questions, context, and methodologies when writing your review so panels can moderate accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see the UK Research and Innovation policy on declarations of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow UKRI’s declarations of interest policy. Declare conflicts promptly and follow the Funding Service procedures for declaring interest or declining to review if conflicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of COVID-19 impacts on track record
rubrics_metrics.description: When undertaking your assessment of the research project, you should consider the unequal impacts of the impact that COVID-19-related disruption might have had on the track record and career development of those individuals included in the proposal, and you should focus on the capability of the applicant and their wider team to deliver the research they are proposing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the project as written and focus on the applicant’s capability to deliver. Known COVID-19 impacts should have been highlighted in the application; do not penalise applicants for pandemic-related disruption. Potential future pandemic-related complications should be treated as post-award issues and should not affect the score given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding how reviews feed into decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are considered by two or more peer reviewers; applicants provide a response (principal investigator response) to the comments of the peer reviewers; proposals, reviews, and principal investigators’ responses to the reviews are considered by the assessment panel; the panel then provide a rank ordered list of proposals in order of funding priority; the panels’ recommendations are considered internally by BBSRC and a final decision is taken on the list of awards to be supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews contribute directly to panel moderation and ranking. Write reviews with the knowledge that panels and applicants (via right to reply) will see and act on your comments; provide clear, evidence-based assessments to support panel decision-making.
